title: Human and Mouse Islet Single-cell Dispersion for Patch-clamp and Imaging
author: Aliya F Spigelman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.spiedke

steps.title: Islet Collection
steps.instruction: Pick islets into a 15 mL falcon tube using as little media as possible.

steps.title: Cell Dissociation
steps.instruction: Dissociate the islets into single cells using Gibco cell dissociation buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of Gibco cell dissociation buffer (cat # 13150-016).
Incubate in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Pipette islets up and down with a 1 mL pipette to produce single cells.

steps.title: Cell Washing and Recovery
steps.instruction: Wash the dissociated cells and prepare them for plating.

substeps.instruction: Add 9 mL of human islet culture media.
Resuspend pelleted cells in human islet media (~200 µL/dish).

steps.title: Cell Plating and Incubation
steps.instruction: Plate the suspended cells and allow them to adhere.

substeps.instruction: Plate a ~200 µL drop of suspended cells in the center of each tissue culture treated 35 mm dish.
Culture at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
After 4 hours, add 2 mL of human islet culture media.

steps.title: Islet Purification
steps.instruction: Hand pick islets to achieve high purity using non-tissue culture treated dishes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer islets into a 10 cm non-tissue culture treated petri dish, adding human islet culture media if needed.

Under a stereomicroscope, hand pick islets into a second 35-mm non-tissue culture treated dish containing human islet culture media (maximum final density of 10 islets/dish; e.g., 60 islets for 6 dishes).
Repeat the picking process into subsequent 35-mm petri dishes until islets reach close to 100% purity.
